.audit/design.md:154:**Versioned legacy raw adapter feeding source-native domain:** detect old UUID-plus-source rows at the raw reader, discard their database IDs, and reconstruct all outputs with source keys. This hides useful compatibility from cleaner/resolver callers and permits API-free replay of populated partitions. It loses because empty old partitions encode only database UUIDs: neither the current rebuilt database nor an unordered member capture establishes their original identity. Correct whole-run replay would require an external historical mapping, partial-cohort semantics, or a fresh API fetch anyway. Those choices add a second migration workflow and expose recovery policy to callers. Never silently skip old empty partitions or infer their source identity from the set difference of members.
.audit/design.md:158:**Selected explicit old-artifact policy:** old raw, old cleaned, and old resolved runs fail before output publication with a clear unsupported-identity-format message directing the operator to capture a new ingestion run, then clean/resolve/load it. Preserve old files unchanged. Do not overwrite a run's artifacts in place or mix raw/new cleaned versions. No automatic legacy adapter in this task. If preserving this specific old capture becomes an explicit requirement, reconsider the versioned boundary adapter plus a complete historical UUID mapping; do not introduce unchecked or partial replay.

The selected design assumes yes and gives an actionable failure for old runs; it does not require a permission checkpoint. Are external artifact consumers relying on the old column names? Migrate repository consumers and document the format break; do not silently preserve UUID-shaped fields.
